title: Audience-led homepage hero playbook
body:
Context:
This is an experiment playbook for homepage hero and first-fold messaging that frames Redwood Inference as the predictable, cost-aware inference runtime developers trust to put in production. The doc is audience-led: we propose distinct hero narratives for three primary segments (Platform teams, AI-native startups, and Enterprise product teams) plus a generic developer-facing default. The goal is to increase trial sign-ups from engineering audiences and increase qualified sales leads for Dedicated/Private by surfacing operational assurances and cost levers up-front.

Objectives and success metrics (90d):
- Lift developer trial conversion (signup -> first API call) by 15% for visitors who view the hero variants.
- Increase demo request rate from enterprise-segment pages by 20%.
- Decrease bounce on the homepage for technical visitors (identified by UA + referral from docs) by 12%.
- Track secondary metric: signups that attach a repo or app token within 7 days.

Audience-specific hero pillars (what matters to them):
- Platform teams: predictable latency, deployment parity across hosted/dedicated/private, rollout controls (canary/A-B/fallback).
- AI-native startups: fastest time-to-outcome, low unit cost, transparent performance claims, easy prototyping -> production path.
- Enterprise product teams: compliance, private deployability (VPC/HSM), SLAs and auditability.
- Generic developer: simple API, fast onboarding, free credits and sample apps.

Hero narrative approach (three levers to combine):
1) Claim (what we promise): short, specific, technical-credible.
2) Proof (how we back it up): micro-metrics + short one-liners about features.
3) Action (what to do next): CTA targeted to audience.

Headline & subhead variants (grouped by audience) -- treat as copy snippets to A/B: 
- Platform teams (bold/technical):
  Headline A: "Serve models with production SLOs — predictable latency, at scale."
  Subhead A: "Unified runtime across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Canary rollouts, fallbacks, and token-level cost visibility."
  CTA A: "Get latency benchmarks"

  Headline B: "Same API in dev, staging, and production — ship with confidence."
  Subhead B: "Pin model versions, route by cost or region, and automate safe rollouts."
  CTA B: "See rollout patterns"

- AI-native startups (velocity + unit-economics):
  Headline A: "Turn prototypes into product features faster — without half your margin."
  Subhead A: "High-throughput runtime, intelligent batching, and model recommendations to cut per-token cost."
  CTA A: "Estimate my per-call cost"

  Headline B: "Prototype quickly, scale cheaply."
  Subhead B: "Free credits, quick SDKs, and cost controls that keep your unit economics healthy."
  CTA B: "Start a free project"

- Enterprise product teams (compliance & control):
  Headline A: "Private inference with enterprise controls and SLAs."
  Subhead A: "Customer-managed VPCs, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit trails — deploy where your data must stay."
  CTA A: "Request an enterprise brief"

  Headline B: "Run inference on your network. Keep compliance in control."
  Subhead B: "On-prem or VPC options plus support and security reviews for regulated workloads."
  CTA B: "Talk to sales"

- Generic developer (simple, direct):
  Headline A: "A faster, predictable API for model inference."
  Subhead A: "Text generation, chat, embeddings — one consistent API across deployments."
  CTA A: "Try the API"

Microcopy hooks and trust lines to test (short blocks under hero):
- "Benchmarked latency for 8k tokens on A100: median 120ms per token (public test)."
- "Save up to 3x on per-token cost with batching + KV caching."
- "SLA-backed Dedicated clusters. Private control plane available."
- Logos/short customer snippets: 1–2 line quotes for speed/cost gains.

Primary CTA experiment matrix (examples):
- CTA text variants: Try the API / Start a free project / Estimate my cost / Request a brief.
- CTA targets: signup flow / landing calc tool / enterprise form / docs quickstart.
- Measurement: conversion funnel by CTA for each audience cohort, time-to-first-API-call, and demo request yield.

Supporting content to surface under hero (short links or cards):
- Quickstart (engineer): 2-step SDK example + expected latency/cost numbers.
- Case study (startup): 60–90s summary + cost improvement numbers.
- Product brief (platform/enterprise): rollout controls, routing policies, and observability.

Competitive framing notes (short bullets for copy/QA):
- Against cloud AI platforms: emphasize cost-aware controls and predictable per-token economics (not just raw model access).
- Against LLM API-only providers: emphasize deployment flexibility (dedicated/private) and rollout/observability primitives.
- Against self-hosted runtimes: emphasize managed ops & smart routing (we handle kernel selection, capacity fallbacks, and SLA-backed capacity options).

Objection handling snippets (for micro-FAQs near hero):
- "What if my model needs special ops?" -> "We support custom model onboarding and provide quantization + kernel recommendations."
- "Is this more expensive than running myself?" -> "For most production workloads we reduce costs via batching, caching, and routing; we’ll show an estimated delta for your workload."
- "Can I keep data on-prem?" -> "Yes — private control plane and on-prem packages are available with enterprise support."

Experiment rollout plan (3-week cadence):
- Week 1: Implement A/B test between Platform Hero A (technical claim) and Generic Hero (default). Measure developer signup conversion.
- Week 2: Swap in Startup Hero B for 20% traffic coming from startup-targeted acquisition channels. Track cost-estimator CTA clicks.
- Week 3: Run enterprise hero to 25% of direct and paid enterprise traffic; swap CTA to 'Request an enterprise brief'.
- Ongoing: Rotate microcopy trust lines weekly, prioritize variants that increase trial->api-call conversion.

Analytics & instrumentation checklist:
- UTM mapping for acquisition source -> audience cohort.
- Event: hero_variant_viewed, CTA_clicked (which CTA), signup_started, first_api_call, demo_requested.
- Dashboard to slice by referral, device, and URL path.

Implementation notes for product/content teams (quick ops):
- Keep headlines < eight words when possible; subheads should include one concrete proof stat if available.
- Provide a 2-line engineering quickstart to display as the first supporting card beneath hero.
- Ensure trust line metrics are backed by internal benchmark pages (link to GTM bench doc).
- Use feature flags to roll hero variants per audience bucket.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Do we surface median latency numbers by default, or require a 'show benchmarks' CTA to reduce complexity?
- Which customer logos are approved for use in first test (need legal sign-off).
- Who owns the enterprise brief content (marketing or solutions engineering)?

Next steps (owners):
- Marcus Li: wire up variant text in the staging site and create feature flags (due 2026-02-18).
- Priya Rao: prepare a short enterprise brief draft and a one-page startup case study (due 2026-02-22).
- Evan Chen: add event tracking and a dashboard template (due 2026-02-25).
- Ava (owner): coordinate legal logo approvals and finalize the first microcopy set (due 2026-02-26).

Notes to self / working extras (scratchpad):
- Consider a mid-hero small interactive: 'estimate per-call cost' that asks two quick questions and returns ballpark. Could double as a lead-gen form for startups.
- If rollout shows strong enterprise demo requests, prepare a Dedicated vs Private quick comparison page.
- Slack thread: #gtm-hero-tests has early feedback; link to key notes in Confluence.
